title-group.article-title: HSPB1 variants in distal hereditary motor neuropathy: two families

sec.title: Introduction
sec.p: Small heat shock protein HSPB1 (HSP27) mutations cause distal hereditary motor neuropathy (dHMN) and axonal Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2F. We describe two unrelated families with HSPB1 variants and variable onset.

sec.title: Case Reports
sec.p: Family 1: The proband was a 42-year-old man carrying a heterozygous c.404C>T (p.Ser135Phe) variant in HSPB1, segregating with an autosomal dominant pattern. Onset of lower-limb weakness was at age 35. Nerve conduction studies showed an axonal motor neuropathy; creatine kinase was mildly elevated at 320 U/L.
Family 2: A 29-year-old woman carried a heterozygous c.250G>A (p.Gly84Arg) variant. Age of onset was 24 years, with distal weakness and pes cavus. Family history was positive across two generations.

sec.title: Genetic and Clinical Findings

caption.p: Clinical and molecular features of the patients.

sec.p: A third patient (Case 3), the aunt of the Family 2 proband, carried the p.Pro182Leu variant with late onset at age 50.

sec.title: Discussion
sec.p: These findings expand the phenotypic spectrum of HSPB1-related neuropathy. The p.Ser135Phe substitution has been reported to reduce chaperone activity.
